# Vultr GPU pricing changes and market comparisons

Vultr maintains the lowest market rate for GH200 at $1.99 per hour, outperforming Spheron. While Spheron offers cheaper A100 PCIe rates, Vultr provides significant savings through 1-year prepaid A100 terms and 3-year committed-use contracts for dedicated access.

 By Technewsdaily September 4, 2026 3 min read 286 views 

## Vultr GPU pricing rates

Vultr sells GH200.

The rate is $1.99.

This price remains the lowest in the current market comparison. DeployBase tracks the 8x HGX H100 80GB bare metal server at $23.92 per hour. This total equals $2.99 per GPU-hour. ComputePrices lists a different H100 SXM rate at $2.30 per GPU-hour. Which figure represents the true cost for an H100? Vultr also sells A100 80GB PCIe instances at $2.397 per hour. This configuration includes 24 vCPUs and 80GB of system RAM. A 1-year prepaid term for an A100 PCIe instance at $2.397 per hour drops the cost to $1.80 per hour, which creates an estimated $5,230 in annual savings at full-time utilization. The A100 SXM rate is $2.60 per hour. This premium covers NVLink interconnect and higher inter-GPU bandwidth. The lineup also includes A40 at $1.86 per hour and A16 at $0.51 per hour. Vultr provides several A16 configurations, including 4-GPU setups at $0.512 per hour and 16-GPU setups at $0.574 per hour. As of December 2025, preemptible AMD MI325X and MI355X plans exist. Users can also secure up to 35% savings on dedicated access with 3-year GPU committed-use contracts.

...

The Spheron on-demand PCIe rate is $1.82 per hour.

Vultr’s A100 PCIe rate is $2.397 per hour. Vultr wins on GH200. The Vultr GH200 rate is $1.99 per hour while Spheron lists it at $3.02 per hour. Spheron provides H100 spot instances at $2.21 per hour for PCIe. This price beats Vultr’s bare-metal per-GPU rate. Vultr lacks a published spot tier for H100. Vultr also lacks a PCIe H100 SKU. The Vultr H100 bare metal node edges out Spheron by 12% on on-demand rates. Spheron’s H100 SXM spot rate is $2.91 per hour. Spheron’s H100 on-demand node rate is $3.38 per hour, while the Vultr node is $2.99 per hour. You can check live rates.

results.title: Vultr Review 2026: GPU by the Hour from $0.47
highlights:
- GPU hourly: A16 $0.471, A40 $1.712, GH200 $1.990, PCIe A100 $2.397 per GPU per hour, with instance totals multiplying by GPU count
- Entry price $2.50/month (1 vCPU, 0.5 GB RAM) is not an application server; the first tier with usable RAM is $6 (1 GB, 25 GB NVMe, 2 TB)
- Dedicated vCPU starts at $30 (4 GB RAM, 30 GB NVMe, 4 TB); the $75 tier gives 150 GB of NVMe, five times General Purpose
- Add-ons: backups +20% of the base fee, snapshot storage $0.05/GB/month, DDoS protection +$10/month for 10 Gbps, Windows licence extra

 Last updated Sep 25, 2026 Pricing verified Sep 25, 2026

...

Every figure here comes from Vultr’s own pricing pages, checked on 25 September 2026. Where a number is the vendor’s marketing rather than a price, it is labelled as a claim rather than repeated as a finding.

...

## The GPU ladder, quoted per GPU per hour

Per-GPU hourly rates from Vultr's own Cloud GPU pricing page, checked 25 September 2026. These are per-GPU rates — an instance's total is the rate multiplied by the number of GPUs in it.

The “per GPU” is the part buyers miss. The A16 is listed in 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16-GPU configurations and the rate is per card, so an 8-GPU A16 instance bills $3.767 per hour. The A40 is $1.712 for one GPU and $6.849 for four; the PCIe A100 is $2.397 for one and $19.178 per hour for eight.

...

The A16 is the lowest entry on the page and is aimed at virtual desktops and light graphics, not at large language model inference. For a remote desktop or a modest rendering job the rate is genuinely low; for a model it is the wrong tier, and buying it because it is cheapest is the predictable mistake.

What the inference lines are. Vultr positions the GH200 at $1.990 per GPU per hour and the PCIe A100 at $2.397 as the compute for model inference — four to five times the A16’s rate, per GPU, per hour. Above them sit multi-GPU-only lines quoted per GPU per hour from $1.85 to $3.50 — AMD’s MI300X at $1.850, NVIDIA’s HGX B300 at $3.500. Those sell as multi-GPU instances, so the per-GPU figure is a unit price, not a bill.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

#### Vultr Cloud GPU and HGX GPU#

Vultr's 2023-2026 GPU expansion is the centerpiece of its enterprise growth story. NVIDIA HGX H100 80GB sits at approximately $2.30-$2.60/GPU-hour on-demand; A100 80GB at approximately $1.40-$1.80/GPU-hour; L40S at approximately $0.90-$1.20/GPU-hour; A40 and A16 at lower economics for lighter inference workloads. Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

## H100 vs H200

The H200 uses the same GH100 die as the H100, so compute throughput is identical. The difference is memory: the H200 replaces the H100's 80 GB of HBM3 with 141 GB of HBM3e, increasing capacity by 76% and bandwidth by 43%.

| Memory Bandwidth | 3.35 TB/s | 4.8 TB/s |
| FP8 Throughput 1 | 3,958 TFLOPS | |
| FP16 / BF16 Throughput 1 | 1,979 TFLOPS | |
| TDP | Up to 700W | |
| Cloud price (on-demand) | $2.99–$12.29/GPU-hr | $3.99–$10.85/GPU-hr |

What is the cheapest NVIDIA H100 cloud provider?

Vultr has the lowest fixed H100 rate at $2.99/GPU-hr as of November 2026. Vast.ai's median was $3.00/GPU-hr on November 8, but that's from 2 hosts listing an H100 and the price changes daily. Hyperbolic ($3.19), Thunder Compute ($3.20) and Lambda ($3.79) follow. Among hyperscalers, AWS is cheapest at $6.88/GPU-hr.

**Ben Pouladian**: Founder, BEP Research | Covering the Co-Design Era of AI.

Nebius notified customers of 17–21% on-demand GPU price increases effective October 1.
For B200, the move from $7.15 to $8.50 per GPU-hour adds $1,350 per 1,000 GPU-hours, before other charges and discounts.
For compute buyers, that makes the applicable region and contract terms worth checking. For investors, a higher posted rate alone does not establish realized pricing, utilization, or margins.
